_meta.description: Hand-authored labeled queries for NEXUS-HEAL retrieval evaluation. 4 queries per runbook (10 runbooks x 4 = 40 queries). Difficulty levels: easy = direct keywords; medium = indirect language; hard = vague/ambiguous; composite = multiple symptoms, may cross-reference multiple runbooks.
_meta.ground_truth_format: relevant_runbooks is a list of runbook filenames (e.g., 'runbook_cpu_spike.md'). Most queries have exactly one relevant runbook; composite queries may have two when symptoms legitimately overlap.
_meta.hard_queries_note: Hard queries are INTENTIONALLY ADVERSARIAL. Several (notably Q03, Q07, Q15, Q19) share little or no domain vocabulary with the target runbook (e.g., Q07 — 'service unresponsive after a day, restart fixes temporarily' — has zero memory-related keywords but is labeled as memory_leak). These queries are designed to probe the ceiling of pure semantic retrieval: they demonstrate where lexical overlap disappears and where production systems would benefit from hybrid dense+BM25 retrieval or query rewriting. Do not relabel or drop them — the failures they surface are intentional evidence of informed design trade-offs.
